reasoning: Each testplan element has one pinned reachability bin and one pinned reference-model check. All referenced signals are declared DUT ports, signal lists contain only output ports, and no check embeds a hard-coded expected value.

bins.condition: nReset and rst are asserted and released, ena is toggled, clk_cnt is exercised at the listed boundary values, cmd is driven through the valid command encodings, and scl_i and sda_i are monitored across the resulting phases
ena is active, cmd is driven through START, STOP, READ, and WRITE, and scl_i is connected to the resolved open-drain bus model while scl_oen is observed
A START waveform is followed by a STOP waveform while sda_i is connected to the resolved open-drain bus model and sda_oen is observed
nReset is inactive, rst is inactive, a valid cmd is active, and cmd, din, scl_i, and sda_i change between successive rising edges of clk
A command is active with nReset inactive and rst transitions to its active state across a rising edge of clk before being released
A command is active and nReset transitions to its active state between rising edges of clk, remains active without a clock edge, and is then released

ena is deasserted for multiple rising edges while cmd holds a START request, clk_cnt selects the stated timing interval, scl_i and sda_i are toggled during the disabled interval, and ena is later reasserted
ena is active, clk_cnt is zero, cmd holds a START request from the idle state, and the request is held through its attempted completion
ena is active and the same START request is executed in separate runs with clk_cnt set to two different nonzero prescaler values while scl_i and sda_i remain idle-high
After reset, scl_i and sda_i each receive an independent short low pulse followed by a sustained low interval, with ena active and the synchronized input history allowed to update
The controller is idle, scl_i is held high, and sda_i transitions from high to low for enough sampled clocks to pass synchronization and filtering
A prior START has made the bus active, no command is active, scl_i is held high, and sda_i transitions from low to high for enough sampled clocks to pass synchronization and filtering
cmd holds a READ request with ena active, scl_oen releases SCL, scl_i is held low by the bus model for multiple filter opportunities, and scl_i is later released
During an active READ high phase, scl_oen is released and scl_i is driven through a falling transition followed by a rising transition
cmd holds a WRITE request with din high, sda_oen releases SDA during the arbitration-check phase, and sda_i is driven low long enough to become filtered before returning high
cmd holds a READ request while the controller is active, scl_i is filtered high, and sda_i is driven from low to high long enough to create an externally observed filtered STOP
cmd holds a READ request with ena active, sda_i is driven low during the released SDA interval, and the low level persists through the filtered scl_i rising transition
cmd holds a READ request with ena active, sda_i is released high during the released SDA interval, and the high level is present at the filtered scl_i rising transition
The bus is idle-high, ena is active, clk_cnt is zero, cmd holds a START request, and the request is held until cmd_ack is observed
A START has occurred, cmd then holds a STOP request, sda_i initially represents a low bus state, and scl_i is allowed to rise through the released SCL phase
ena is active, clk_cnt is zero, din is low, cmd holds a WRITE request, sda_i remains externally released during the arbitration-check phase, and cmd is held through completion
ena is active, clk_cnt is zero, din is high, cmd holds a WRITE request, sda_i remains externally released during the arbitration-check phase, and cmd is held through completion
While the controller is idle with ena active and clk_cnt zero, cmd is driven through NOP and each listed unsupported command encoding

checks.expr: scl_o and sda_o match the constant-drive reference model throughout reset, idle, command phases, and input changes
scl_oen and the sampled scl_i behavior match the resolved open-drain SCL reference model in every command phase
sda_oen and the sampled sda_i behavior match the resolved open-drain SDA reference model through the START and STOP phases
All registered outputs match the post-posedge reference model and show no registered transition between rising-edge updates
The registered outputs match the synchronous-reset reference model after the qualifying posedge, with active state unchanged before that edge and no stale command response afterward
The outputs match the asynchronous-reset reference model immediately on the nReset transition and retain reset-state behavior until a new valid command is accepted
Every output during ena-disabled clocks matches the hold-and-reload reference model, and the subsequent enabled command sequence matches the resumed timing model
The START phase waveform and completion pulse match the clk_cnt-zero reference model, with phase changes occurring only on eligible timing events
Both nonzero-prescaler START runs match the divider reference model for phase order, transition spacing, and completion timing without intervening phase changes
The outputs match the synchronized three-sample filter reference model for glitch suppression, sustained transitions, protocol decisions, and filtering latency
busy matches the reference model after the filtered SDA falling transition while filtered SCL is high
busy and al match the reference model after the filtered SDA rising transition while filtered SCL is high and no non-STOP command is active
The READ high-phase wait, subsequent phase order, and completion pulse match the stretch-aware reference model and do not complete before filtered SCL release
Phase-transition timestamps and completion timing after the external SCL fall match the synchronized shared-clock reference model with divider reload at the detected fall
The arbitration-loss assertion, command abort, output release, absence of completion acknowledgment, sticky status, and reset clearing match the reference model
The outputs match the filtered unexpected-STOP reference model for arbitration status, bus status, idle return, output release, and suppression of acknowledgment
dout capture, output-enable phase order, and the completion pulse match the filtered READ reference model for the sampled SDA condition
dout capture, output-enable phase order, and the completion pulse match the filtered READ reference model for the sampled SDA condition
The accepted START output-enable sequence and single completion pulse match the ordered FSM reference model
The accepted STOP output-enable sequence, filtered-SCL-high wait, bus-status update, and completion pulse match the STOP reference model
The WRITE data-drive phase, SCL phase order, arbitration status, and completion pulse match the reference model for the applied din condition
The WRITE data-release phase, SCL phase order, arbitration status, and completion pulse match the reference model for the applied din condition
The output enables and acknowledgment behavior for every NOP and unsupported command interval match the idle reference model
